parts.headline: Nvidia’s Demand Is Real. Its Financing Is Fragile.
The Model Is Not the Price

mentions.excerpt: Graham Rhodes of Longriver, whose fund has owned Nvidia since 2025, changes the unit of account.

Longriver Investment Partners Limited, in its July 20 letter, relayed an annualized run-rate at Anthropic of $1 billion at the end of 2024, $9 billion at the end of 2025 and almost $50 billion in May, as proof that customers pay for agentic work.
Longriver's run-rate was judged in direct contradiction with three managers of the same season.
Longriver's Anthropic run-rate was almost $50 billion in May.

mentions.section: The buyers have not paid yet
mentions.excerpt: Longriver Investment Partners warned in its July 20 letter that AI can transform business and still fail its builders, because revenue can arrive well before owner earnings.

Longriver Investment Partners Limited told clients on July 20 that Anthropic's reported annualized revenue went from about $1 billion at the end of 2024 to almost $50 billion in May 2026, evidence in its view that customers will pay for agentic work.

Longriver's almost $50 billion in May had become about $65 billion by August, a figure that Tae Kim of Key Context wrote on August 21 the market treated as a disappointment; he called that an overreaction, since the growth rate was still extremely high.
